title: Projects
intro: Selected work across privacy-first developer tools, cloud identity systems, AT Protocol product development, and agent-assisted software delivery.

records.title: utills.dev — Private Browser Utilities
records.copy:
A live privacy-first developer tools app for formatting, decoding, validating, converting, and asking questions about everyday engineering data: JSON, YAML, XML, JWTs, Base64, URLs, hashes, regexes, and character encodings. The standard utilities run locally in the browser, so sensitive payloads and tokens can stay on the user's machine.

The app also includes tool-aware AI chat. JSON, JWT, Base64, YAML, XML, regex, hash, and encoding pages can pass the current working context into an embedded assistant. It defaults to Chrome's in-browser Prompt API / Gemini Nano when available, with bring-your-own-key fallback for OpenAI, Anthropic, or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Built as a production-quality utility suite: React 19, strict TypeScript, Vite SSR prerendering across 21 routes, Tailwind CSS v4, SEO/reference guides, GitHub Actions deployment to S3/CloudFront, 345 unit tests, and 181 Playwright E2E tests across five browsers.
records.summary: Privacy-first browser utilities with contextual AI chat for JSON/YAML/XML, JWT, Base64, regex, hashes, URLs, and encoding workflows.
highlights: Keeps sensitive tokens and payloads local while supporting JSON/YAML/XML conversion, JWT verification, and Base64 URL-safe workflows.
Adds contextual AI chat using Chrome's in-browser Prompt API/Gemini Nano when available, plus BYOK OpenAI, Anthropic, and custom endpoint options.
Shipped with 345 unit tests, 181 Playwright E2E tests across five browsers, and GitHub Actions deployment to AWS S3/CloudFront.

records.title: OCI IAM: Admin Surfaces, APIs, and Observability
records.copy:
Professional engineering work at Oracle Cloud Infrastructure across identity administration, authentication, OAuth/session APIs, SDK generation, observability, and production reliability for enterprise cloud customers.

Built customer-facing React console surfaces for Dynamic Groups, Policies, Reports, and Applications; designed a metadata-driven reports UI that reduced duplicated frontend work; implemented Java REST APIs for MySessions visibility and session-management workflows; improved authentication observability for a high-scale identity platform; refactored canary infrastructure to cut alert noise by 50%; and strengthened release/on-call practices that reduced regressions by 20%.

Also led cross-functional delivery of OCI Identity Domains SDK generation across Python, Java, and Go by rewriting Swagger generation for legacy endpoints, authoring architecture documents, aligning senior identity stakeholders, and creating examples that helped enterprise developers adopt the platform.
records.summary: OCI identity engineering across admin UX, Java APIs, OAuth/session workflows, SDK generation, observability, and production reliability.
highlights: Built React console surfaces and metadata-driven IAM reports for Dynamic Groups, Policies, Reports, and Applications.
Implemented Java session-management APIs and authentication observability for high-scale identity workflows.
Cut canary alert noise by 50%, reduced regressions by 20%, automated multi-region deployment effort by 60%, and led SDK generation for Python, Java, and Go.

records.title: Multi-Agent Development Workflow
records.copy:
A practical agent-assisted development workflow for turning ambiguous software work into constrained, inspectable delivery loops. The system separates research, implementation, and review so AI assistance is scoped by evidence, acceptance criteria, validation, and human judgment.

The workflow uses role-specific agents for read-only scouting, vertical-slice implementation, and standards/spec review; dispatch tooling for isolated specialist runs; optional sequential chains; visible status dashboards; scoped tool access; retry handling; clean-worktree rules; and durable decision/handoff notes for context recovery.

The project is less about asking an LLM to write code and more about engineering the trust boundary around it: task decomposition, acceptance criteria, dependency modeling, validation gates, retry limits, output scoring, and review checkpoints.
records.summary: Agent-assisted coding workflow with scout/builder/reviewer roles, dispatch tooling, validation gates, and review checkpoints.
highlights: Defines a repeatable scout → builder → reviewer workflow with scoped tools and vertical-slice delivery rules.
Uses specialist dispatch, sequential pipelines, session isolation, and dashboard-style status visibility to keep work inspectable.
Combines validation gates, retry limits, output scoring, durable handoffs, and human review boundaries.

records.title: SheerVue - AT Protocol Social Client
records.copy:
A third-party AT Protocol social client built with React Native, Expo, and TypeScript. SheerVue focuses on social reading and control: transparent moderation surfaces, developer-friendly post rendering, quieter feed controls, and AT Protocol features that extend beyond a single default client experience.

Built across iOS, Android, and Web with production React Native patterns: TanStack Query server state, persisted preferences, cross-platform file resolution, custom feed APIs, typed AT Protocol lexicon integration, OAuth-first third-party sign-in boundaries, native module integration, and a full product rebrand.

Key features include soft-block transparency and a Blocked Me feed, fenced code blocks and inline code rendering, per-account repost hiding, repost deduplication, minimalist reading-focused feed mode, thread collapsing/unroll concepts, cross-app AT Protocol badges, and account-management guardrails appropriate for a third-party OAuth client.
records.summary: Third-party AT Protocol client with soft-block transparency, code-aware posts, repost controls, OAuth boundaries, and reading-focused feeds.
highlights: Builds differentiated AT Protocol client features: soft-block transparency, Blocked Me feed, code blocks, per-account repost hiding, and repost deduplication.
Delivers cross-platform React Native/Expo architecture across iOS, Android, and Web with TanStack Query, persisted preferences, and typed AT Protocol APIs.
Defines third-party-client boundaries around OAuth sign-in, account-management surfaces, moderation visibility, and cross-app AT Protocol identity.

title: Earlier Projects
intro: Earlier React and JavaScript projects from my transition into software engineering.

records.title: Packing Planner
records.copy:
Packing Planner provides a pre-populated, customizable packing checklist based on the climate the user will be travelling to and the activities they expect to participate in. The final checklist is saved to browser local storage.

Technologies used: JavaScript, CSS, JSON, arrays, local storage.
records.summary: Bootcamp-era packing checklist app using JavaScript and local storage.

records.title: One-Bar
records.copy:
One-Bar is an SMS-based application that lets users in areas with limited mobile coverage access vital information such as weather forecasts, hospital locations, restaurants, local trails, and news. A Node.js server receives requests via Twilio, calls third-party APIs, parses data, and relays information back to the user.

Technologies used: Node.js, Express, Superagent, EJS, PostgreSQL, Twilio, Google Maps, Yelp, Dark Sky, Hiking Project, News API.
records.summary: Bootcamp-era SMS information service for low-connectivity travel scenarios.

records.title: CF Quick-Start
records.copy:
cf-quick-start is a globally installed NPM package that generates starter code for Node.js project types including API servers, Express servers, React apps, and socket servers with tests and configuration files.

Technologies used: Node.js, NPM packages, Inquirer, fs, fs-extra, Jest.
records.summary: Bootcamp-era npm package for generating Node.js starter projects.

records.title: BuzzCard
records.copy:
BuzzCard is a mobile application that allows users to exchange contact information by scanning QR codes. Users create a profile, choose what to share, and a QR code is dynamically generated for another user to scan.

Technologies used: React Native, Expo, Redux, Babel.
records.summary: Bootcamp-era React Native QR contact-sharing application.
